SWEET DECEPTION

By: Joy Summers | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Tonight on Carte Blanche we reveal how much of the honey you buy may be fortified with sugar, corn or rice syrup.

Unique Selling Point:
A consumer story with a twist

Summary:
In a recent international documentary expose it was revealed how Chinese honey has made its way into the homes of many consumers around the world. Nothing wrong with that, except that it's not pure honey. Its honey bolstered by rice and corn syrup to make it go further.

And South Africa it seems is no different, warns Agbiz agricultural economist Wandile Sihlobo
While sold as '100% natural honey', some Chinese honey also contains antibiotics that can be dangerous to humans.


Further information:
Worryingly, South Africa imports massive amounts of Chinese honey, says Sihlobo.
Statistics from the International Trade Commission (based on SA Revenue Services data) show that imports of Chinese honey to South Africa have rocketed from 20 tonnes in 2001 to 3,577 tonnes last year. South African bee producers deliver 2,000 tonnes per annum.
Some 85% of honey imports to South Africa now come from China. This has come at the cost of New Zealand, whose exports to SA fell from 300 tonnes to 3 tonnes between 2001 and 2017.
"What is truly alarming is that people who are eating honey because of its lower glycaemic index, may be inadvertently consuming huge amounts of sugar," says Sihlobo

Sihlobo says some of the honey brands available in South Africa are improbably cheap. "Given the high cost of beekeeping due to dying bee populations, this is further evidence that the honey we buy may be mixed with syrup."
Turn to the labels on some of the honey sold in PnP - its packed in South Africa but where your honey comes from is unclear. According to the packaging it could be Brazil, it could be Zambia or China.
At Sally Williams they have come up against the great honey deception. Their last container of Nougat was rejected by the European Union because South Africa cannot say for certain what is in its honey. This is forcing the company to use Zambian honey which has the requisite paperwork.
However, Bomikazi Molapo, spokesperson for the department of agriculture, forestry and fisheries, says that the department is not aware of any Chinese honey which is not compliant with SA regulations.
"The department applies, in a consistent and uniform manner, regulatory controls to all imported products from all countries importing to South Africa. There are regulatory controls against which honey is subjected to, including compositional tests in terms of the Agricultural Product Standards Act 119 of 1990. Not only Chinese honey but all imported honey is subjected to the same control."
So what is happening on the ground here in South Africa? Well down in Hilton, the home of Hilton Honey farms all is not well. According to two people familiar with what is happening, Mr Roland Kennard has been buying up all the small honey farmers, is bottling honey under a variety of labels, diluting the honey with sugar syrup and selling it on to you the unsuspecting consumer. Peels Honey and Struckmeiers are just two of his labels.
Denver Jardine used to work for Kennard and when he challenged him, apparently he was threatened with his life…so Jardine said nothing.
But Peter Nicholson, a beekeeper and honey farmer is not prepared to keep quiet and will speak to Carte Blanche about the great honey deception.

Press Release:


Consumers who choose to pay a premium for honey, seen as a healthier sugar substitute with natural antioxidants, enzymes and amino acids, are in for a rude awakening. Carte Blanche investigates the largescale adulteration of honey and finds out how to check if you are buying pure honey or a version with sugar syrups added. And, as honey adulteration proliferates, we ask why is there a complete lack of food quality enforcement from the government agency meant to police our honey.

Script:


Sweet Deception Final script TX 29 July 2018 - mix script

Commentary One
Raw pure honey, straight from the hive and into the bottle. Healthy, delicious and a great sugar alternative

Up sound buzz

That's what you think you are buying in every bottle of honey. But the shocking news is that the bad boys of South Africa's honey trade are adulterating your honey with cane sugar.

Mike
I want to show you this honey Devi, that was given to us that is clearly adulterated honey

Commentary Two
Mike Miles is chairman of the South African bee industry organisation or SABIO

Mike
you can see how the honey has separated - here at the top is pure syrup, here at the bottom is granulated honey I suppose.

Commentary Three
Concerned about the reputation of the industry, SABIO, a voluntary organisation of genuine honey producers, has been asking government to police the honey adulterators who are deceiving the South African public

Mike
So, if I can show you this honey as well. This honey is also adulterated, you can see the syrup at the top. Have a look at it.
Devi
They are very clever, it just says natural honey
Mike
Does it say where it comes from, who is the bottler?
Devi
Produced by Grandis apiaries

Link
Its DAFF the Department of Forestry and fisheries that are supposed to police honey. But
speak to the beekeepers, and they say DAFF isn't doing its job

Commentary four
So the only way the industry can be certain that honey is adulterated is to send it overseas for testing. But when DAFF said they had no money, big industry players like Brett Falconer stepped in. Brett spends fortunes testing his imported honey both before and after it is shipped.



Brett Falconer Highveld honey
We decided as industry to sponsor government to do these tests, but we had a suspensive condition, that we wanted them to act and do something when they found the culprits

Commentary Five
Eight samples were sent overseas, 6 out of the 8 failed the tests. But the department, says SABIO, is dragging its feet

Mike
They say we don't have the finances to follow up, so we are at a dead end

Link
You have to be really enthusiastic about your job to get up this early on a cold winter morning and set off on a journey looking for adulterated honey

Commentary six
We were on our way to the Midlands, home to some of the oldest honey labels in the country. Peels honey has been around since 1924 and is currently part owned and managed by Craig Campbell. He is determined to rid the industry of fake honey

Craig Campbell
It makes one really annoyed because we are trying to sell a product that we are really proud of

Commentary seven
Peels is also battling to compete against fake honey

Devi
So you can get honey for R40 rand what is your response to that?
Craig
I would be very suspicious of that honey

Commentary eight
But cheap honey is being sold across the country. So how do you know? The best tests measure the quantity of C3 and C4 sugars. C4 sugars are derived from sugar cane and grasses, and C3 sugars from nectar, beet and rice sugars. High levels of these sugars are not naturally found in pure honey.

Devi
Now let me get this straight the international acceptance level of C4 is 7%?
Mike
Yes or less
Devi
This one came back as 67.1 and this one 26.5
Devi
So it may look like honey, it may smell like honey but is not honey- that is adulterated honey.

Mike
Its honey in inverted comma's

Commentary nine
Both those honeys came from the Midlands - the honey that was 67.1 syrup came from Grandis Apiaries owned by Roland Kennard, and the honey that is 26.5% syrup comes from here - Hilton Honey farms. Owner Rob Beach.

Devi
The honey you import, how do we know that honey is not adulterated?
Rob
That is a good question, um, I buy honey from reputable firms. I do occasional tests.
If someone is adulterating in their plant…
Devi
You won't know
Rob
I wouldn't know. I do the taste test, and I do the colour and I do the viscosity

Commentary ten
But in a world of honey adulteration that's no longer enough, and the test on Rob Beach's honey puts it squarely into the category of adulterated honey
Devi
So, I am glad you are sitting down, because a test was done, and it came up at 26.5% for C4 sugar.
Rob
Hmm. I am surprised.
Devi
What does this mean now?
Rob
I am not sure. I must look into it.

Commentary eleven
It's also mandatory under South African law to say on the bottle, which country, honey comes from. Many of the samples we inspected, don't give that information, and neither does the honey here at Hilton Honey farms

Devi
In terms of your honey does it say on the bottle where it comes from?
Rob
No
Why?
Rob
Maybe I am remiss in putting it on the label, but the honey generally arrives here granulated and I change its form and in changing its form it becomes my product.
Devi
Yeah but it didn't come from you?
Rob
No, I don't say it comes from me, I say bottled by Hilton Honey farms
Devi
But you don't say where it comes from at all?
No
Devi
According to labelling laws are you right or wrong?
Rob
I admit that I am probably wrong
Devi
Shame, not probably, you are wrong!
Rob
I am wrong ya, I can change that.
Devi
You don't have to because I am asking!
Rob
Because it's wrong, ya.

Commentary twelve
Since we did this interview, Hilton Honey farms have redesigned their labels.

LINK
Our understanding, from the available evidence is that if we are looking to find at least one of the sources of adultered honey, its right here behind these gates

Commentary thirteen
This is Grandis Apiaries where Roland Kennard, produces his honey. The floors of his shed were wet - it had obviously been sprayed down ahead of our arrival.

Devi
for some reason your name keeps coming up when we talk about adulteration of honey - what is up with that?
Roland
Well if you are trying to sell your honey at R65 per bottle and you have a competitor who is selling it at R40 per bottle you are not going to like that. …and there has always been fierce competition in the honey market for market share

Commentary fourteen
Roland Kennard's honey, Struckmeiers can be found on the shelves for R39 99. Its labelled guaranteed pure honey

Devi
Well that is the allegation, the reason why you can sell it at R40 a bottle is because you are adulterating it. Are you doing that?
Roland
No, I am not. I am feeding my bees, but I am not putting anything into my honey - adulterant into the honey

Commentary fifteen
40 000 squeezy bottles of Kennards honey are packed monthly, but he also supplies other packers who put their own labels onto his honey. Labels like Honey bee and Asal

Roland
It's my honey but he buys from me, in other words, I supply him the unlabeled honey. Yes that is my honey.

Commentary sixteen
Kennard claims he is an innovator and a business man

Roland
And I like stretching the boundaries in creativity

Commentary seventeen
But just how far is Kennard stretching the boundaries? Quite far, it seems according to a whistleblower who said he cooked up Roland's honey for 3 years. He asked us to hide his identity

"John"
Okay I'll explain step by step. Firstly, we pour water into a big pot. Each pot takes six containers of water. And then we add sugar into the same pot, forty-eight bags, into each pot to cook. And then there are drums, those two hundred litre ones, we mix the cooked sugar in there and remove it in the morning to make it like honey. That's how we do it.

Devi
How much of sugar
John
48 bags into one pot
Devi
That's a lot of sugar!
John
Yes. Every week, on a day like today, we receive a truck of sugar from Makro, Maritzbug. Ten pallets.

Commentary eighteen
Could that explain then, why Kennard's honey Struckmeiers, tested way above the 7% limit?

Mike with Roland's honey
Well this again, it's been tested as syrupy, and I am giving you a good dollop, so you can taste that
Devi pulls her face
That's syrup!



Commentary nineteen
We then showed Roland the industry tests done on his honey that registered 59.2 and 67% sugars.

Devi
I am talking about your honey. It's not pure honey, this is what I am saying can only go on these
Roland
But this is international regulations.
Devi
Why should it not apply to us?
Roland
It isn't incorporated into our law
Devi
It should be maybe?
Roland
It should be but it hasn't been
Devi
I would be worried about that test?
Roland
This is high I admit
Devi
It's not just high, it's too much of high

Commentary twenty
Roland Kennard said his honey complied with South Africa's sucrose limit of 5%. He also said he hadn't been around when the tests were done.

Roland
I am not happy with those results
Devi
I am sure you are not, but do you think there is something wrong with the results
Roland
No, no, no, no, no - what I need to do is to change the method that I am producing the honey at. The method. Change the method.

Commentary twenty-one
But what method? Don't Roland's bees make his honey? No, according to John

John
Then after boiling…Most of the times they wake us up around two am and we cook the stuff up to around eleven or twelve o'clock, around those hours in the afternoon. That's when we take it off and it would have become like porridge.


Commentary twenty-two
John says they also add lemon juice to the mixture

John
We pour in two bottles of lemon juice into the one big pot. When it boils until it looks black, we take it off. In the middle of the night it then turns to look like honey.

Devi
Do you add lemon juice to your honey?
Roland Kennard
No, what we do is we make up a feed for our bees, and we add a certain amount of lemon juice to break up the sucrose in the feed.

Commentary twenty-three
Kennard implied that the lemon juice he fed his bees was somehow finding its way into the honey. He also blamed his suppliers

Devi
When I chose your honey off the shelf
Roland
I am not blaming them…
Devi
I expect you to do all the checks and balances I don't expect to one day do an interview with you and you say I don't know what went into it
Roland
No….
Devi
Then why am I paying you for the honey if you don't even know what went into it?
Roland
Does the taste of the honey mean anything to you when you buy honey?

Commentary twenty-four
To convince us his honey was pure, Mr. Kennard invited us to a honey tasting the following day. But we postponed our appointment to make a detour after a tip off. Here, about 2 kilometres from his premises lay piles of dumped sugar. Kennard cancelled our later appointment.

Devi Link
You are not going to believe me but behind me are piles of sugar, bags of syrup and an entire drum filled with strange sticky stuff - you have to come and have a look

Commentary twenty -five
Strange coincidence or an indication of a cover up. But in an email Kennard says he has no knowledge of the dumping incident and resents the implication



Devi
So, you are going to say no one has ever done mixing, ever, no lemon juice, no palettes of sugar arriving from Makro that has never happened?
Roland
No I am not saying that, I have tried many different things with honey, I have tried feeding bees, manipulating swarms to expanding my bees

Commentary twenty-six
To confirm the findings of the two previous tests done on Kennards Struckmeiers honey, we did our own test, on this bottle bought in Howick a day after the interview.

Up sound: "its sealed."

Commentary twenty-seven
This week our results came back from Germany. It failed the tests. At 44% syrup, it is far from the pure honey, guaranteed on the label.

Devi
So the worst I can accuse you of is feeding bees with sugar
Roland
Yes that is the worst they can accuse me of.

Commentary thirty
So as the money flows, excuse me, the honey flows, adulterators profit, and the only plan DAFF has on the table is to outsource their responsibility as regulators to private companies.
DAFF also want to charge the honey producers for the tests - a move SABIO says will cripple them. And they say, DAFF's proposed tests still won't stop the honey adulterers. DAFF declined an interview.

BRETT
the tests proposed are a joke! Syrup would pass those tests they are not testing for authenticity of honey they are doing test for irrelevant stuff that syrup would pass

THE END 14 12

PROMO ONE 10 seconds
Is the honey you are buying everything it says on the label? The shocking news is that the bad boys of South Africa's honey trade are adulterating your honey with cane sugar.

PROMO TWO 15 seconds
Internationally Honey is one of the top ten food products subject to food fraud. We put our local honey producers to the test.
Devi
So the worst I can accuse you of is feeding bees with sugar
Roland
Yes that is the worst they can accuse me of.




PROMO THREE

Commentary
When last did you look at the label on the back of the honey you buy.
Devi
According to labelling laws are you right or wrong?
Rob
I admit that I am probably wrong
Devi
Shame, not probably, you are wrong!
Rob
I am wrong ya, I can change that.


PROMO FOUR

Roland
Now how do I know that the honey I have purchased doesn't have the high C4
Devi
When I chose your honey off the shelf
Roland
I am not blaming them…
Devi
I expect you to do all the checks and balances I don't expect to one day do an interview with you and you say I don't know what went into it
Roland
No….
Devi
Then why am I paying you for the honey if you don't even know what went into it?
Roland
Does the taste of the honey mean anything to you when you buy honey?

No Devi According to labelling laws are you right or wrong? Rob I admit that I am probably wrong Devi Shame, not probably, you are wrong! Rob I am wrong ya, I can change that. Devi You don't have to because I am asking! Rob Because it's wrong, ya. Commentary twelve Since we did this interview, Hilton Honey farms have redesigned their labels. LINK Our understanding, from the available evidence is that if we are looking to find at least one of the sources of adultered honey, its right here behind these gates Commentary thirteen This is Grandis Apiaries where Roland Kennard, produces his honey. The floors of his shed were wet - it had obviously been sprayed down ahead of our arrival. Devi for some reason your name keeps coming up when we talk about adulteration of honey - what is up with that? Roland Well if you are trying to sell your honey at R65 per bottle and you have a competitor who is selling it at R40 per bottle you are not going to like that. …and there has always been fierce competition in the honey market for market share Commentary fourteen Roland Kennard's honey, Struckmeiers can be found on the shelves for R39 99. Its labelled guaranteed pure honey Devi Well that is the allegation, the reason why you can sell it at R40 a bottle is because you are adulterating it. Are you doing that? Roland No, I am not. I am feeding my bees, but I am not putting anything into my honey - adulterant into the honey Commentary fifteen 40 000 squeezy bottles of Kennards honey are packed monthly, but he also supplies other packers who put their own labels onto his honey. Labels like Honey bee and Asal Roland It's my honey but he buys from me, in other words, I supply him the unlabeled honey. Yes that is my honey. Commentary sixteen Kennard claims he is an innovator and a business man Roland And I like stretching the boundaries in creativity Commentary seventeen But just how far is Kennard stretching the boundaries? Quite far, it seems according to a whistleblower who said he cooked up Roland's honey for 3 years. He asked us to hide his identity "John" Okay I'll explain step by step. Firstly, we pour water into a big pot. Each pot takes six containers of water. And then we add sugar into the same pot, forty-eight bags, into each pot to cook. And then there are drums, those two hundred litre ones, we mix the cooked sugar in there and remove it in the morning to make it like honey. That's how we do it. Devi How much of sugar John 48 bags into one pot Devi That's a lot of sugar! John Yes. Every week, on a day like today, we receive a truck of sugar from Makro, Maritzbug. Ten pallets. Commentary eighteen Could that explain then, why Kennard's honey Struckmeiers, tested way above the 7% limit? Mike with Roland's honey Well this again, it's been tested as syrupy, and I am giving you a good dollop, so you can taste that Devi pulls her face That's syrup! Commentary nineteen We then showed Roland the industry tests done on his honey that registered 59.2 and 67% sugars. Devi I am talking about your honey. It's not pure honey, this is what I am saying can only go on these Roland But this is international regulations. Devi Why should it not apply to us? Roland It isn't incorporated into our law Devi It should be maybe? Roland It should be but it hasn't been Devi I would be worried about that test? Roland This is high I admit Devi It's not just high, it's too much of high Commentary twenty Roland Kennard said his honey complied with South Africa's sucrose limit of 5%. He also said he hadn't been around when the tests were done. Roland I am not happy with those results Devi I am sure you are not, but do you think there is something wrong with the results Roland No, no, no, no, no - what I need to do is to change the method that I am producing the honey at. The method. Change the method. Commentary twenty-one But what method? Don't Roland's bees make his honey? No, according to John John Then after boiling…Most of the times they wake us up around two am and we cook the stuff up to around eleven or twelve o'clock, around those hours in the afternoon. That's when we take it off and it would have become like porridge. Commentary twenty-two John says they also add lemon juice to the mixture John We pour in two bottles of lemon juice into the one big pot. When it boils until it looks black, we take it off. In the middle of the night it then turns to look like honey. Devi Do you add lemon juice to your honey? Roland Kennard No, what we do is we make up a feed for our bees, and we add a certain amount of lemon juice to break up the sucrose in the feed. Commentary twenty-three Kennard implied that the lemon juice he fed his bees was somehow finding its way into the honey. He also blamed his suppliers Devi When I chose your honey off the shelf Roland I am not blaming them… Devi I expect you to do all the checks and balances I don't expect to one day do an interview with you and you say I don't know what went into it Roland No…. Devi Then why am I paying you for the honey if you don't even know what went into it? Roland Does the taste of the honey mean anything to you when you buy honey? Commentary twenty-four To convince us his honey was pure, Mr. Kennard invited us to a honey tasting the following day. But we postponed our appointment to make a detour after a tip off. Here, about 2 kilometres from his premises lay piles of dumped sugar. Kennard cancelled our later appointment. Devi Link You are not going to believe me but behind me are piles of sugar, bags of syrup and an entire drum filled with strange sticky stuff - you have to come and have a look Commentary twenty -five Strange coincidence or an indication of a cover up. But in an email Kennard says he has no knowledge of the dumping incident and resents the implication Devi So, you are going to say no one has ever done mixing, ever, no lemon juice, no palettes of sugar arriving from Makro that has never happened? Roland No I am not saying that, I have tried many different things with honey, I have tried feeding bees, manipulating swarms to expanding my bees Commentary twenty-six To confirm the findings of the two previous tests done on Kennards Struckmeiers honey, we did our own test, on this bottle bought in Howick a day after the interview. Up sound: "its sealed." Commentary twenty-seven This week our results came back from Germany. It failed the tests. At 44% syrup, it is far from the pure honey, guaranteed on the label. Devi So the worst I can accuse you of is feeding bees with sugar Roland Yes that is the worst they can accuse me of. Commentary thirty So as the money flows, excuse me, the honey flows, adulterators profit, and the only plan DAFF has on the table is to outsource their responsibility as regulators to private companies. DAFF also want to charge the honey producers for the tests - a move SABIO says will cripple them. And they say, DAFF's proposed tests still won't stop the honey adulterers. DAFF declined an interview. BRETT the tests proposed are a joke! Syrup would pass those tests they are not testing for authenticity of honey they are doing test for irrelevant stuff that syrup would pass THE END 14 12 PROMO ONE 10 seconds Is the honey you are buying everything it says on the label? The shocking news is that the bad boys of South Africa's honey trade are adulterating your honey with cane sugar. PROMO TWO 15 seconds Internationally Honey is one of the top ten food products subject to food fraud. We put our local honey producers to the test. Devi So the worst I can accuse you of is feeding bees with sugar Roland Yes that is the worst they can accuse me of. PROMO THREE Commentary When last did you look at the label on the back of the honey you buy. Devi According to labelling laws are you right or wrong? Rob I admit that I am probably wrong Devi Shame, not probably, you are wrong! Rob I am wrong ya, I can change that. PROMO FOUR Roland Now how do I know that the honey I have purchased doesn't have the high C4 Devi When I chose your honey off the shelf Roland I am not blaming them… Devi I expect you to do all the checks and balances I don't expect to one day do an interview with you and you say I don't know what went into it Roland No…. Devi Then why am I paying you for the honey if you don't even know what went into it? Roland Does the taste of the honey mean anything to you when you buy honey? metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Tonight on Carte Blanche we reveal how much of the honey you buy may be fortified with sugar, corn or rice syrup.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: A consumer story with a twist
metadata.Summary: In a recent international documentary expose it was revealed how Chinese honey has made its way into the homes of many consumers around the world. Nothing wrong with that, except that it's not pure honey. Its honey bolstered by rice and corn syrup to make it go further. And South Africa it seems is no different, warns Agbiz agricultural economist Wandile Sihlobo While sold as '100% natural honey', some Chinese honey also contains antibiotics that can be dangerous to humans.
metadata.Further information: Worryingly, South Africa imports massive amounts of Chinese honey, says Sihlobo. Statistics from the International Trade Commission (based on SA Revenue Services data) show that imports of Chinese honey to South Africa have rocketed from 20 tonnes in 2001 to 3,577 tonnes last year. South African bee producers deliver 2,000 tonnes per annum. Some 85% of honey imports to South Africa now come from China. This has come at the cost of New Zealand, whose exports to SA fell from 300 tonnes to 3 tonnes between 2001 and 2017. "What is truly alarming is that people who are eating honey because of its lower glycaemic index, may be inadvertently consuming huge amounts of sugar," says Sihlobo Sihlobo says some of the honey brands available in South Africa are improbably cheap. "Given the high cost of beekeeping due to dying bee populations, this is further evidence that the honey we buy may be mixed with syrup." Turn to the labels on some of the honey sold in PnP - its packed in South Africa but where your honey comes from is unclear. According to the packaging it could be Brazil, it could be Zambia or China. At Sally Williams they have come up against the great honey deception. Their last container of Nougat was rejected by the European Union because South Africa cannot say for certain what is in its honey. This is forcing the company to use Zambian honey which has the requisite paperwork. However, Bomikazi Molapo, spokesperson for the department of agriculture, forestry and fisheries, says that the department is not aware of any Chinese honey which is not compliant with SA regulations. "The department applies, in a consistent and uniform manner, regulatory controls to all imported products from all countries importing to South Africa. There are regulatory controls against which honey is subjected to, including compositional tests in terms of the Agricultural Product Standards Act 119 of 1990. Not only Chinese honey but all imported honey is subjected to the same control." So what is happening on the ground here in South Africa? Well down in Hilton, the home of Hilton Honey farms all is not well. According to two people familiar with what is happening, Mr Roland Kennard has been buying up all the small honey farmers, is bottling honey under a variety of labels, diluting the honey with sugar syrup and selling it on to you the unsuspecting consumer. Peels Honey and Struckmeiers are just two of his labels. Denver Jardine used to work for Kennard and when he challenged him, apparently he was threatened with his life…so Jardine said nothing. But Peter Nicholson, a beekeeper and honey farmer is not prepared to keep quiet and will speak to Carte Blanche about the great honey deception.
